title: 56% of US Workers Spend Whole Workday Indoors
paragraphs: Many office workers spend almost all of their working day inside, without stepping outside even once. According to a new survey, this is true for more than half of American hybrid workers.
The survey was carried out by Talker Research for Wild Planet, a food company. It asked 2,000 hybrid workers, who work some days in the office and some days at home, about their lunch habits.

The survey found that 56% of workers usually stay inside for the whole day when they go to the office, apart from their trip to and from work. Many also skip lunch. In fact, 85% said they sometimes skip their lunch break completely. On average, workers eat lunch at their desks about 2.5 days a week.

Even during lunch, many people do not really take a break from screens. On average, workers spend 61% of their lunch break looking at a device. Many use this time to check social media, read messages or even reply to work emails.
So why don't people go outside? The most common reasons were having too many meetings or tasks, chosen by 29%, and feeling pressure to always be available to colleagues, chosen by 25%.
However, most workers know that breaks are important. About 91% said a lunch break is essential, and 78% said that, in an ideal world, they would eat lunch outside on most workdays.

Eating outside seems to make people happier. Before eating lunch outside, 51% of workers rated their happiness as four or five out of five. After eating outside, that number rose to 66%. In addition, 64% said fresh air helps them to focus again.
Sue Thanavaro of Wild Planet said that taking just a few minutes to change your surroundings and get some fresh air can make a big difference.
